title: Central multiplicative preimages in smooth connected group extensions
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme]. An $S$-group scheme has multiplication, identity and inverse satisfying the group diagrams; a homomorphism respects them. A group of multiplicative type of finite presentation is an fppf-local form of $D(M)=\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_S[M]$ for a finitely generated abelian group $M$, with $e_m\mapsto e_m\otimes e_m$ as comultiplication [def-sfb-ring-diagonalizable-group]. Fppf means faithfully flat and locally of finite presentation [def-pc-fppf-site]. Let $H,J$ be smooth affine $S$-groups of finite presentation with connected geometric fibres [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] [def-weil-connected-scheme]. Let $q:H\to J$ be a faithfully flat finitely presented homomorphism whose scheme-theoretic kernel $N$ is central and of multiplicative type. Central means that all its points commute with all group points after every further base change. If $D\hookrightarrow J$ is a closed central subgroup of multiplicative type of finite presentation, then $q^{-1}(D)=H\times_JD$ is a central subgroup of $H$ of multiplicative type of finite presentation. This is a scheme-theoretic assertion, commutes with arbitrary base change, and does not require $N$ or $D$ to be smooth.

source.place: Lemma 3.3.1(2) and proof, printed pp.96--97. Applied to an arbitrary smooth connected affine group, without reductivity. WANTED locally as literature/conrad-reductive-group-schemes.pdf.

proof.text: Put $E=H\times_JD$ and let $p:E\to D$ be the second projection. The group operations restrict to this fibre product because $D$ is a subgroup and $q$ is a homomorphism; its kernel is $N$. By [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change], $E\hookrightarrow H$ is a closed immersion. It is affine by the affine-chart characterization in [def-weil-closed-immersion]; composing with the affine structure morphism of $H$ gives $E\to S$ affine by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-composition]. The singleton $\{q:H\to J\}$ is an fppf covering, and [lem-trf-fppf-covering-base-change] gives the fppf covering $\{p:E\to D\}$. In particular every section of $D$ lifts to $E$ after an fppf covering.

source.place: Lemma 3.3.1(2), proof, printed p.97: preimage and quotient; Stacks Tags 01QR, 01SC, 021O for the scheme-theoretic permanence used here.

proof.text: For sections $h\in H(T)$ and $x\in E(T)$ define $c(h,x)=hxh^{-1}x^{-1}$. Since $q(x)\in D(T)$ is central in $J(T)$, $q(c(h,x))=1$, so this is a morphism $H\times_SE\to N$. If $p(x)=p(y)$ then $y=xn$ for $n=x^{-1}y\in N(T)$; centrality of $N$ gives $c(h,xn)=c(h,x)$. Thus this morphism agrees on both projections from the relation of $H\times_SE\to H\times_SD$. This latter map is an fppf covering by [lem-trf-fppf-covering-base-change], hence fpqc by [lem-trf-fppf-covering-is-fpqc]. Descent [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-representable-descent] supplies a unique morphism $b:H\times_SD\to N$ with $b(h,p(x))=c(h,x)$. All these identities are identities on arbitrary scheme-valued points, not just geometric points.

source.place: Lemma 3.3.1(2), proof, printed p.97: map to the Hom-functor via a local lift; Stacks Tags 021O, 022C and 023Q for descent.

proof.text: For $x,y\in E(T)$, the centrality of $c(h,x),c(h,y)\in N(T)$ gives $c(h,xy)=c(h,x)c(h,y)$ by expanding $hxyh^{-1}(xy)^{-1}$. After lifting two sections of $D$ along the fppf cover $p$, this identity proves $b(h,d_1d_2)=b(h,d_1)b(h,d_2)$, and $b(h,1)=1$. Equality descends by [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-representable-descent], with the needed pulled-back coverings provided by [lem-trf-fppf-covering-base-change] and [lem-trf-fppf-covering-is-fpqc]. Thus $b$ is an $H$-family of group homomorphisms $D\to N$. At the identity section of $H$ this homomorphism is zero because $c(1,x)=1$.

source.place: Lemma 3.3.1(2), proof, printed p.97: explicit commutator calculation underlying its Hom-functor; Stacks 023Q for equality descent.

proof.text: Work locally on an affine open of $S$ and choose successive fppf covers splitting $D$ and $N$. Refine the first covering by affine schemes using [lem-pc-fppf-affine-refinement], and then refine a splitting cover for $N$ over each resulting affine base in the same way. Base change of these coverings is permitted by [lem-trf-fppf-covering-base-change]. Over one such affine base $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$, write $D_U=D_A(M)$ and $N_U=D_A(L)$. Since $H_U$ is affine, $b$ is a homomorphism between the split diagonalizable groups with character groups $M,L$ over the affine scheme $H_U$. By [lem-sfb-relative-diagonalizable-character-duality], it is described by a locally constant function on $H_U$ with values in $\operatorname{Hom}(L,M)$. On each connected geometric fibre of $H_U\to U$ this function is constant; that fibre contains its identity point, where the value is zero by step 3. Every point lies under a geometric fibre, so the function is zero everywhere. The quoted character-duality theorem, including its validity over nonreduced rings, implies $b=1$ as a morphism over $U$. Successive uniqueness descent [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-representable-descent], using [lem-trf-fppf-covering-is-fpqc], gives $b=1$ globally.

source.place: Lemma 3.3.1(2), printed p.97, Hom-functor rigidity; direct character-duality variant using Appendix B.1, printed pp.280--281, instead of reducing to finite torsion; Stacks 021P for affine refinement.

proof.text: Consequently $c(h,x)=b(h,p(x))=1$ for every $T,h,x$, and this remains true after every further base change. Thus $E$ is central in $H$, in precisely the functorial sense of the statement, and in particular $E$ is commutative. Apply [lem-sfb-relative-commutative-multiplicative-extension] to $p:E\to D$: $E$ is affine by step 1, $p$ is faithfully flat and locally of finite presentation by that step, its kernel is $N$, and both ends have the stipulated multiplicative type. This proves that $E$ has multiplicative type of finite presentation.

source.place: Lemma 3.3.1(2), proof, printed p.97, last use of Corollary B.4.2(2), printed pp.299--301.

proof.text: For any $S'\to S$, the fibre-product universal property identifies $(H\times_JD)\times_SS'$ with $H_{S'}\times_{J_{S'}}D_{S'}$, including its group operations and inclusion in $H_{S'}$. The centrality just proved was tested on all scheme-valued points and therefore already asserts centrality after this change of base. Pull back the fppf covers on which $E$ has the prescribed diagonalizable presentation; they remain coverings by [lem-trf-fppf-covering-base-change]. The Hopf formulas pull back to the identical formulas on the group algebras of the new base, so this proves the multiplicative-type assertion there. In particular neither this argument nor any preceding step assumes that $N$ or $D$ is smooth.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q09-f7df4a22f (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Read the item's statement and all six steps, the new node, and the statements of all 14 cited nodes. Not a re-split delivery (no repair order) and the item statement is unchanged. Conrad (3.3.1(2), B.4.2(2)) is not in the local literature and is recorded as WANTED, so I checked the mathematics directly. Step 1: E=H×_J D is a closed immersion into H by 01QR, affine by the chart criterion in def-weil-closed-immersion and 01SC, and p:E→D is an fppf covering by 021O(3); ker p=N. Step 2: q(c(h,x))=1 because D is central in J; c(h,xn)=c(h,x) because N is central in H; the commutator descends to b:H×D→N along the fpqc covering by 022C and 023Q (target an arbitrary scheme). Step 3: c(h,xy)=c(h,x)c(h,y) by centrality, and the identity descends by two uniqueness descents. Step 4: on affine splitting pieces (021P refinement), the existing character-duality node gives a locally constant u:L→M on the nonempty affine H_U, valid for nonreduced rings; u is 0 on the identity section and constant on each connected geometric fibre, so u=0 everywhere and b=1, then uniqueness descent globalizes. This is Conrad's Hom-rigidity made explicit. Step 5: E is central, hence commutative, and every hypothesis of the new node holds (E affine, p flat, surjective and lfp, N fp as a base change of q). Step 6: base change of the fibre product and of the splitting covers. Edge cases: D=1, N=1, S empty; the Q8 example over C shows the connected-fibre hypothesis is essential. New node: statement-only, self-contained, every notion cited. I believe it is true (commutative case of SGA3 XVII 7.1.1 / Conrad B.4.2, via local exactness of the character sheaf and Cartier duality). Tested on mu_{p^2} over F_p[eps] and on a commutative extension of Z/l by G_m; the Heisenberg group shows commutativity is needed. It is the relative generalization of the field node lem-sfb-commutative-multiplicative-type-extension, not a duplicate or a restatement of the item. I swept the 138 multiplicative-type nodes; Mathlib has no such theorem. Batch-5 flags: lem-trf-fppf-covering-base-change (021O) and lem-trf-fppf-covering-is-fpqc (022C) are generic topology facts outside both assumptions and are not steps of the trace-formula or Poincare-duality proofs; character-duality reaches the trace-formula chapter only through generic 022C. Accepted. tool_uses: lem-pc-fppf-affine-refinement is accepted as a generic off-unit tool. No fixes.
